My new book, Co-Existence, is out today.  It is a guide to how to live & work in a world where AI is sometimes, but not always, better than you.

(And, for the release, I worked with Opus 5.5 to make a quite interesting experience for the book's website:
New test of which organizations have low AI capability: you haven’t updated your apps for the iPhone Duo yet.

As I have written many times in the past years, any potential financial downturn in AI stocks will not greatly change the AI trajectory

AI is not going away, companies are not slowing down adoption nor is development slowing. We still need policy & effort so that AI is used well

Whatever role AI played as an issue in this election, I suspect it will play a larger role in every election to come, at least for the foreseeable future.

AI semiotics: cool paper suggests that AIs are strongly impacted by visual symbols in ways they do not always recognize in their own chains-of-thought. The way they react to those symbols is very different than how a human might interpret them as well.
Thanks to all my Dutch readers and @AlexanderNL, my incredible publisher there, for making the Dutch translation of Co-Existence the #1 non-fiction book in the Netherlands!

The AI slopcomments are out-of-control on X but also remarkably easy to stop if the company wanted to?

I did a little experiment and found that combining as few as five comments and running them through Pangram is good enough to weed out the slop and not punish real humans.
